summary: The candidate eliminates cross-request logits amplification and prevents the reviewed 40-byte allocation from exceeding a 4-byte budget, but an atomic request-local row larger than the budget raises RuntimeError instead of completing safely. This is a validated partial allocation fix, not a full fix for the original all-ranks availability failure, and the reported B300/CUDA serving workload was unavailable.

tests.command: PYTHONPATH=/job/repo/python /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-280f586142c9/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_dsa_kpool_mqa_logits_chunking.py test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_dsa_kpool_grouped_chunking.py (candidate tests checked out over recorded base 358c163250ad3b1f62939b01ce1314a0a31a0365)
tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before: 8 failed and 1 passed. The base made one 240-byte cross-request logits output against a 24-byte budget and lacked request grouping and the atomic-row guard.
12 passed on one gfx950 GPU with real FP8 and metadata tensors; DeepGEMM and top-k were mocked to measure call shapes, budgets, and mapping orchestration.
4 independent adversarial cases: 40-byte row under a 4-byte budget is rejected before the kernel, while budgets 40, 41, and 79 bytes admit exactly one 40-byte atomic row without exceeding the budget.

gpu_evidence: One AMD Instinct MI355X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm7.2, HIP 7.2.26015. Source imports resolved under /job/repo/python. GPU tensors were real; DeepGEMM and fused top-k were mocked.
remaining_counterexamples: If one request's group.k_rows * 4 exceeds logits_budget_bytes, the candidate raises RuntimeError on the DSA path. It prevents an over-budget allocation but does not produce top-k output or demonstrate that TP workers survive, so the original all-ranks availability contract remains unresolved for this boundary.

The early num_q * num_k < 8000000 return bypasses memory-budget inspection. A sub-threshold fp32 logits allocation can still be attempted regardless of currently free memory; this was source-inspected but not claimed as a reproduction of the reported 73.65 GiB case.
remaining_limitations: No four-B300 CUDA TP=4/EP=4 system was available; testing used one AMD gfx950 GPU.
No GLM-5.3-Flash or RadixArk model weights were available.
Hierarchical-cache, DFLASH, multi-request 300K-1M context serving traffic, and worker survival were not reproduced.
DeepGEMM and fused top-k were mocked, so NVIDIA kernel allocation behavior and end-to-end numerical correctness remain unverified.
No native files changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
